description: A BBS-themed view of the Warez page. The file area lists every file in the index as numbered rows (name, kind, real install count, a two-line brief, no id line) with [upd!] and [inst] markers; every menu letter filters or sorts it, l lists the top ten by measured installs, / searches, and r redials the index (the cached listing stays on screen under a NO CARRIER banner while it is offline).
examples: Open Warez for the very first time: the modem dials, the logo draws and docks, and the main menu appears under the node box. Every later visit shows the normal Warez page.
Press any key during the dial-up to skip it, then press a menu letter to see it echoed at the main menu prompt.
Press g to hang up: NO CARRIER shows, any key dials again, Esc goes back to Warez.
Open /#elite/board to land on the board with no dial-up.
Press s for skills only, i for installed only, then d to sort by downloads; the counts on the FILES and STATE panels follow what you narrowed.
Press / and type a word, Enter lists the matches over every kind, Esc clears the search and shows everything again.
Press l for the top ten by measured install counts; a file whose count could not be read is left out, never shown as zero.
how_to: Open Warez from the menu: the first time ever you land in Elite Access. After that, click the gray pi in the bottom-right corner of the Warez menu (on a phone, the bottom-right of the menu screen).
Any key or click skips the dial-up. On a page opened without a click, the first key or click starts the sound.
Alt+D dials again, Alt+H hangs up, Esc returns to Warez.
Use /#elite for the dial-up and /#elite/board to go straight to the board.
In the board: a s t m p pick a kind, i v u n narrow by state, f w o e d c sort, l the top ten, / searches, : or the Command line takes a typed command, r redials the index.

Enter opens the FILE_ID.DIZ of the file under the bar (a sheet on a phone), Shift+= adds or updates it, = tries it, Shift+M comments, Alt+Up and Alt+Down scroll the pane, Shift+D downloads, Shift+U updates and Shift+C clears the tagged files, ? lists every key.
